title: Ibn al-Qaysarani to the compiler of a Mamluk book of cipher verses, about 1330-1370 (Penn LJS 51, f. 106v)

steps.what: Fetched the master TIFF of f. 106v from OPenn by plain curl and cut line crops.
Transcribed the seven lines sign by sign from the crops; about 35 shapes on the first pass.
Read the red letters over the first five signs as waw nun alif ayn sin; with the sixth sign as ta marbuta the first word is wa-na'isa.
The group of four signs ending alif-nun recurs three times, once followed by ha-alif: ajfan, wa-ajfani, wa-ajfanuha. Gave jim, fa, ha and the lam-alif sign.
Took the damaged word at the end of line 2 as jahannam and the next as a four-letter word in h-j.
Scanned line 1 as a tawil hemistich (qad ja'ala l-hawa) and used the metre to fix the second hemistich: laha muhjati mathwa wa-khaddi laha arda.
Read the triangle-bar-loop sign of lines 4 and 7 as ayn (a'ta, mu'ta).
Separated that sign from ayn as ra: arda, sahirtu, marda; wa-lam anam, wa-namat wa-lam tashad gave mim, ta, dal.
Read the last open word, four signs in line 5, as sihah from sense and metre; merged the shapes to 22 signs, all with values.

Viewed ff. 105r-106r: other writers, other alphabets, each with its plaintext; f. 106r has the compiler's remark on another message that lam-alif was made one letter. No alphabet was compared sign by sign.
Two exact-phrase web searches for the two verses.
Checked that all four hemistichs scan as tawil, that both verses rhyme in -da, and that the key is one-to-one over 22 signs.

validation.notes: No Arabic language model in lang/, and 89 signs over 22 types with six signs occurring once

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The entry was a red gloss over the first five signs of the cipher (five letters); the other 17 signs were recovered from repeated words, the tawil metre and the rhyme. No plaintext of the message survives and no reading was found.
outcome.fraction_read_source: transcription.txt decoded with key.json (decode.py): 89 of 89 cipher signs have a value; unit cipher signs
outcome.notes: Grades count doubtful signs only: C the five glossed signs, M the three damaged signs of line 2, I four signs read from the word (O, J, the D of ja'ala, the last sign of sihah). The other 77 signs are read from the recovered key and are not graded.

texts.label: Penn LJS 51, f. 106v: two verses

reading_review.note: Two complete verses; all four hemistichs scan as tawil and the rhyme holds.

texts.summary: Two love verses in the tawil metre sent in cipher by Ibn al-Qaysarani to the compiler of the volume: love has made the poet's heart the dwelling of a drowsy-eyed girl and his cheek the ground beneath her; he lies awake with sound eyelids while she sleeps with 'sick' ones. The compiler's own solution was on a leaf now lost.

prior.where: The compiler solved it in the 14th century but the leaf with his plaintext is lost. Catalogue vetting of 15 Nov 2026 found no study or reading (Penn TEI, Digital Scriptorium, DECODE, Tomokiyo, Lasry's list, web); two exact-phrase web searches for the verses on 16 Nov 2026 found nothing.
